funding: Ongoing support from Arts Council England, Southwark Council, the Bukhman Foundation, Bloomberg Philanthropies and Garfield Weston Foundation, plus trusts, commercial galleries and individual patrons; charity income £2.33M in the year to March 2025.
why_flagged: SLG returned a £125,000 Mortimer and Theresa Sackler Foundation gift in 2018; it also takes Bloomberg Philanthropies money, which advocacy groups target elsewhere.
other_findings: The Mortimer and Theresa Sackler Foundation offered £125,000 in 2016 for an education centre in the fire station project; trustees voted to return it in 2018 (The Art Newspaper, 2019).
The Bukhman Foundation, which funds Art Block, is financed by the Playrix mobile games fortune of Igor and Dmitry Bukhman (The Art Newspaper, 2025); no controversy reported.
In May 2026, 261 artists, in a letter published via Artists for Palestine UK, asked five London theatres (not SLG) to drop Bloomberg Philanthropies.
Unverified: Artists for Palestine UK (advocacy group) alleges Bloomberg Philanthropies trains Israeli settlement officials through the Bloomberg-Sagol Centre at Tel Aviv University.
bottom_line: SLG is a long-running public gallery funded by Arts Council England, Southwark Council, trusts and art-world patrons. It returned a Sackler gift in 2018. Worth watching: Bloomberg Philanthropies, which advocacy groups target over Israel links, though not at SLG.

funding: Tate group income £167.15M in 2024-25, including £41.4M DCMS revenue grant-in-aid and £12.5M capital grant; the rest is self-generated, with corporate partners including Bank of America, Hyundai Motor (to 2036), UNIQLO, Bloomberg and LVMH, plus philanthropic donors.
why_flagged: BP's 26-year sponsorship ended in 2017 after years of protest, though BP cited business conditions; Tate removed the Sackler name in 2022 after the P.A.I.N. campaign.
other_findings: BP announced on 11 March 2016 that its Tate sponsorship would end in 2017, citing an 'extremely challenging business environment'; Liberate Tate had staged repeated protests (The Art Newspaper).
BP gave Tate £4m between 1990 and 2006, disclosed in January 2015 after a freedom of information case (The Art Newspaper).
In early 2022 Tate removed the Sackler plaque at Tate Modern and planned to rename the Sackler Octagon at Tate Britain, after the P.A.I.N. campaign (Artnet).
Tate ran a deficit of nearly £9m in 2022-23, and in 2025 DCMS assured its going-concern status while it cut about 7% of staff (Civil Society, Arts Professional).
funders: Department for Culture, Media and Sport
bottom_line: Tate Modern is a public museum funded partly by government grant and largely by self-generated income, with a long roster of luxury, finance and tech sponsors. It ended its BP and Sackler ties after campaigns. Worth watching: its financial strain, and which corporate partners it keeps.
